chapter.name: Integrals
chapter.blurb: Integral calculus is motivated by the problem of finding a function whose derivative is given and by the problem of finding the area bounded by the graph of a function, which lead to the indefinite and the definite integral. The chapter studies indefinite and definite integrals and their elementary properties, including the techniques of integration by substitution, partial fractions and parts, and connects the two through the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

scope_in.item: Explain integration as the inverse process of differentiation: anti derivatives (primitives), the family F(x) + C, the constant of integration and the notation integral of f(x) dx
Use the table of standard integrals (x^n with n != -1, 1/x, e^x, a^x, sin, cos, sec^2, cosec^2, sec tan, cosec cot, and the inverse trigonometric forms)

Apply the properties of indefinite integrals (sum, constant multiple, linear combination; d/dx of an integral) and find anti derivatives by inspection, including a particular anti derivative from a condition such as F(0) = 3
Integrate by substitution x = g(t), including the standard results for tan x, cot x, sec x and cosec x
Integrate squares, cubes and products of sines and cosines using double angle, triple angle and product to sum identities

Use the six standard integrals with x^2 - a^2, a^2 - x^2, x^2 + a^2 and their square roots, and extend them to 1/(ax^2 + bx + c), 1/sqrt(ax^2 + bx + c) and (px + q) over these by completing the square and splitting the numerator
Integrate proper and improper rational functions by long division and the partial fraction forms of Table 7.2, including substitution followed by partial fractions
Integrate products by parts, choosing the first and second function, including log x, inverse trigonometric functions, e^x sin x and integrals of the form e^x [f(x) + f'(x)]
Use the special integrals of sqrt(x^2 - a^2), sqrt(x^2 + a^2) and sqrt(a^2 - x^2), and of sqrt(ax^2 + bx + c) after completing the square
Interpret the definite integral with lower and upper limits, the area function A(x), and state the first and second fundamental theorems of integral calculus
Evaluate definite integrals as F(b) - F(a) and by substitution with changed limits
Use properties P0 to P7 of definite integrals, including modulus integrands, even and odd functions and the add-the-two-forms technique
Solve miscellaneous integrals combining the above methods

concepts.name: Integration as anti differentiation: indefinite integrals, standard formulae and properties
concepts.description: Integration as the inverse process of differentiation: anti derivatives, the constant of integration, the indefinite integral notation, the table of standard integrals, the properties of indefinite integrals, the method of inspection and finding a particular anti derivative from a given condition.
concepts.idea: If F'(x) = f(x), then every function F(x) + C has derivative f(x), so the indefinite integral of f is a whole family of anti derivatives differing by a constant.
concepts.rule: integral of f(x) dx = F(x) + C where F'(x) = f(x); integral of x^n dx = x^(n+1)/(n+1) + C (n != -1); integral of (1/x) dx = log|x| + C; integral of [k1 f + k2 g] dx = k1 integral of f dx + k2 integral of g dx.
concepts.example: integral of (x^3 - 1)/x^2 dx = integral of (x - x^(-2)) dx = x^2/2 + 1/x + C.

concepts.name: Integration by substitution
concepts.description: Changing the variable of integration (x = g(t)) to reduce an integral to a standard form, including the standard results for integrals of tan x, cot x, sec x and cosec x obtained by substitution.
concepts.idea: If the integrand contains a function together with its derivative, putting that function equal to t turns the integral into a simpler one in t.
concepts.rule: Putting x = g(t), dx = g'(t) dt, so integral of f(x) dx = integral of f(g(t)) g'(t) dt. Standard results: integral of tan x dx = log|sec x| + C, cot x -> log|sin x| + C, sec x -> log|sec x + tan x| + C, cosec x -> log|cosec x - cot x| + C.
concepts.example: integral of 2x sin(x^2 + 1) dx: put t = x^2 + 1, dt = 2x dx, giving integral of sin t dt = -cos(x^2 + 1) + C.

concepts.name: Properties of definite integrals
concepts.description: Properties P0 to P7 of definite integrals (change of variable name, reversing limits, splitting the interval, the a + b - x and a - x replacements, the 2a properties, and even and odd functions on [-a, a]) and their use to evaluate integrals, including modulus integrands.
concepts.idea: Many definite integrals that are hard to integrate directly can be found by rewriting them with a property and adding the new form to the old one.
concepts.rule: P1: integral from a to b = -integral from b to a. P2: split at c. P3: integral from a to b of f(x) dx = integral from a to b of f(a + b - x) dx. P4: integral from 0 to a of f(x) dx = integral from 0 to a of f(a - x) dx. P6: integral from 0 to 2a of f = 2 integral from 0 to a of f if f(2a - x) = f(x), and 0 if f(2a - x) = -f(x). P7: integral from -a to a of f = 2 integral from 0 to a of f if f is even, and 0 if f is odd.
